region: Western Pacific — northern Queensland & Papua New Guinea to the Solomon Islands & Vanuatu
description: Told apart from the near-identical ocellaris by its 10 (not 11) dorsal spines and much thicker black borders around the white bars. In the wild it lives mainly in magnificent and giant carpet anemones.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa, Madagascar & Comoros; also the Andaman Sea, Sumatra, Java & Bali
description: Pale orange with a single white stripe along the top of the back from the snout to the tail and no head bar. It lives in magnificent and Mertens' carpet anemones and is one of the gentlest clownfishes.

region: Western Pacific — Gulf of Thailand & Indonesia to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Peach-pink with a narrow white bar behind the head and a white stripe along the ridge of the back. Pairs live mostly in magnificent anemones and rarely stray more than a few centimetres from the tentacles.

region: Western Pacific — Christmas Island & Indonesia to the Solomon Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands
description: Deeper orange than the other skunk clowns, with the white back stripe running forward onto the upper lip. It usually lives in Mertens' carpet anemone and is the most assertive of the skunk group.

region: Indian Ocean — Maldives, Lakshadweep & Sri Lanka
description: Amber-orange with one narrow white head bar and black pelvic and anal fins, hence its other name, blackfoot anemonefish. It lives almost exclusively in the magnificent anemone (Heteractis magnifica).

region: Indo-West Pacific — Persian Gulf & Maldives to Micronesia, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: The most widespread anemonefish and the only one recorded from all ten host anemone species; body colour ranges from yellow-orange to nearly black, but the three white bars are constant. A strong swimmer that ventures farther from its anemone than most clowns.

region: Northern Indian Ocean — Arabian Peninsula & Maldives to India, Sri Lanka, the Andaman Sea & Java
description: Dark brown with an orange-yellow face and belly, two white bars and a yellow tail. Despite its name it lives only in Haddon's carpet anemone (Stichodactyla haddoni) on sandy bottoms, not in the "sebae anemone".

region: Western Pacific — Gulf of Thailand & the Philippines to the Solomon Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands
description: Named for the white saddle that rises from mid-flank into the dorsal fin; the dark tail has a white margin. Pairs live in carpet and leathery anemones on open sand and silty bottoms.

region: Southwestern Pacific — subtropical eastern Australia, Lord Howe & Norfolk Islands
description: Instantly recognised by its extremely broad white mid-body band on a dark brown body with a white head bar and yellow fins. A subtropical species living in leathery anemones (Heteractis crispa), and rarely exported.

region: Southwestern Pacific — Lord Howe Island, Middleton & Elizabeth Reefs
description: Dark brown to black with a single white head bar and a whitish tail; endemic to the Lord Howe Island area, where it lives in bubble-tip anemones. Seldom seen outside Australia.

region: Western Pacific — eastern Indonesia & New Guinea to Fiji, Vanuatu & the Great Barrier Reef, north to the Marshall Islands
description: Red-orange with one white head bar and a large dark patch covering most of the flanks; the pelvic and anal fins are black. In the wild it is closely tied to bubble-tip anemones, often in large family groups.

region: Western Pacific — Gulf of Thailand & southern China to the Ryukyu Islands, Philippines & Indonesia
description: Bright tomato-red with one narrow white bar behind the eye, edged in black on adults; mature females develop a dark smudge on the flanks. It typically hosts the bubble-tip anemone and is far more aggressive than the ocellaris.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Malaysia, Sumatra & Java
description: Orange-red with a large black saddle blotch on the rear flank and no white bar as an adult; juveniles carry a white head bar that fades with age. It lives in bubble-tip and leathery anemones.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — northwestern Australia (Kimberley coast & Northern Territory)
description: A north-western Australian member of the tomato-clown group: dusky red-orange with a single white head bar and a dark brown to black patch over the flanks. It lives in bubble-tip and giant carpet anemones and is only occasionally exported.

region: Southwestern Pacific — Fiji, Tonga & Samoa
description: Described only in 2008, this Fijian member of the tomato-clown complex is bright red-orange with one white head bar and lacks the dark flank patch of its relatives. Mostly found in bubble-tip anemones.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden, also the Chagos Archipelago
description: The Red Sea's only anemonefish: yellow-orange to brownish with two dark-edged white bars and a yellow tail. It uses several host anemones, most often bubble-tip and magnificent anemones.

region: Western Pacific — New Guinea & the Great Barrier Reef to Fiji, Tonga, Samoa, Micronesia & French Polynesia
description: A large, dark brown anemonefish with two bluish-white bars, orange fins and a pale tail. It shelters in big anemones such as Heteractis magnifica and Mertens' carpet anemone.

region: Western Pacific — Great Barrier Reef & Coral Sea to New Caledonia & the Loyalty Islands
description: Very like Clark's clownfish but brown to orange-brown with only two white bars and a whitish tail. It lives in several large anemones on the Great Barrier Reef.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Kenya to Durban, South Africa
description: An East African clarkii-group anemonefish with a dark brown body, orange snout and belly, two white bars and a distinctive white tail fin. It lives in bubble-tip and other large anemones and is exported mainly from Kenya.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Mauritius (Mascarene Islands)
description: Endemic to the Mascarene Islands, this dark brown clarkii-group anemonefish has a golden-orange snout and belly (chrysogaster means "golden belly") and three white bars. Rarely exported.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Seychelles & Aldabra
description: A clarkii-group anemonefish from the Seychelles with three white bars and, as its name says, a dusky brown tail fin with a pale margin. It lives in Mertens' carpet anemone and is rarely exported.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Madagascar & the Comoros
description: Dark brown with an orange-yellow snout and belly, a white head bar and a very wide white mid-body bar; the tail fin is yellow. One of the rarest clownfishes in the hobby.

region: Northwestern Indian Ocean — coast of Oman
description: Found only along the coast of Oman: brown with an orange snout, two white bars (the rear one broad) and a pale tail. It lives among anemones on rocky reefs and is seldom exported.

region: Central Pacific — Marshall Islands
description: Restricted to the Marshall Islands, it ranges from orange-brown to nearly black with three narrow white bars and orange on the snout and fins. It lives in several large anemones in lagoons and on outer reefs.

region: Western Pacific — northern Papua New Guinea & the Solomon Islands
description: Orange with a white back stripe that joins a partial white "bonnet" over the head. Genetic studies show it is a natural hybrid of the orange-fin and orange skunk clownfishes, found only where both parents occur.

region: Indo-West Pacific — western Indonesia & the Andaman Sea to Taiwan, Vanuatu & the Great Barrier Reef
description: The largest and most aggressive clownfish, recognised by a sharp spine below each eye (now often placed in Amphiprion as A. biaculeatus); dark maroon females can be twice the length of their brighter red males. In the wild it lives only in the bubble-tip anemone.

region: Captive-bred; from a naturally melanistic population near Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia
description: A naturally black form of the ocellaris from around Darwin, Australia, now bred in captivity: juveniles are orange-brown and darken to jet black with three bold white bars as they mature. Behaviour and care match the orange form.

region: Captive-bred
description: A line-bred ocellaris whose white bars are enlarged, ragged and partly merged into irregular "snowflake" shapes, still outlined in black. No two fish are patterned exactly alike.

region: Captive-bred
description: Produced by crossing the snowflake line with black (Darwin) ocellaris: a dark brown-to-black fish carrying large, irregular snowflake-style white markings. Young fish show more orange, which darkens with age.

region: Captive-bred
description: A designer ocellaris in which the white has spread to cover almost the whole body, leaving orange on the snout and fins, which keep their black margins.

region: Captive-bred
description: A line of ocellaris in which white covers nearly the entire body and much of the fins; only a wash of orange remains around the snout and pectoral fins, and the black fin margins are retained.

region: Captive-bred
description: A mutation that suppresses the white bars, leaving a plain orange fish with only its black fin margins; some individuals show a faint trace of the head bar.

region: Captive-bred
description: A line-bred ocellaris whose white bars are incomplete — broken, or stopping short of the back or belly — giving each fish an irregular, one-of-a-kind look.

region: Captive-bred
description: A black ocellaris strain in which the bars are reduced to one or two large white spots, usually on the head, like the pips of a domino.

region: Captive-bred
description: An all-black ocellaris with no white bars at all — in effect a "naked" black ocellaris — line-bred from black stock.

region: Captive-bred
description: Line-bred from percula with irregular, enlarged white markings that merge across the flanks, each heavily outlined in black; the most prized "full Picassos" are mostly white.

region: Captive-bred
description: A designer percula in which the white has spread over almost the whole body, leaving orange on the snout and fins; the thick black fin margins of the percula remain.

region: Captive-bred; from naturally heavily pigmented percula of Papua New Guinea & the Solomon Islands
description: Line-bred from the naturally heavily pigmented percula of Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands: the black borders around the white bars spread across much of the body and fins, leaving an orange fish heavily overlaid with black.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Sumatra; widely captive-bred
description: A natural colour form from Sumatra whose bars, white in juveniles, turn golden-yellow and broaden as the fish matures. It was once described as a separate species, Premnas epigrammata.

region: Captive-bred; descended from a wild fish collected in Papua New Guinea
description: Descended from a single wild-caught maroon from Papua New Guinea whose white bars branched into jagged, lightning-like streaks; the trait proved heritable and is now produced in captivity.

region: Captive-bred
description: A captive-bred line derived from gold-stripe maroons in which the golden bars break up and spill into irregular gold flakes and blotches across the maroon body.

region: Indo-West Pacific — eastern Indian Ocean to Micronesia, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Brilliant electric blue; in many populations males have an orange-yellow tail and snout, while females have a clear tail and a black spot at the rear base of the dorsal fin. Males guard eggs laid in rock crevices and defend them fiercely.

region: Western Pacific — Philippines, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea & the Solomon Islands
description: Electric blue with a bright yellow tail; one of the least aggressive damsels. In the wild it lives among branching corals in sheltered lagoons and bays.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Indonesia & northwestern Australia (Rowley Shoals, Scott Reef)
description: Bright blue on the head and upper body and vivid yellow below, the boundary running diagonally back from the snout. Lives on sheltered reefs among branching corals.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines
description: A small electric-blue damsel with a black line running from the snout through the eye to the front of the dorsal fin. It shelters between the branches of Acropora and Pocillopora corals.

region: Southwestern Pacific — New Caledonia & Vanuatu to Fiji, Tonga & Samoa
description: Electric blue above with a yellow belly, anal fin and tail; a South Pacific relative of the blue devil and just as territorial. Common in shallow lagoons around coral and rubble.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Fiji & Tonga, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: A small, mild-mannered damsel with a pale lilac-grey body, a yellow head and a black spot on the soft dorsal fin. It lives on reef slopes and drop-offs, often deeper than other Chrysiptera.

region: Western Pacific — Andaman Sea & Indonesia to New Caledonia
description: Dark slate-blue over the head and front half, with a whitish rear body and tail; one of the more peaceful Chrysiptera. It lives near the bottom on rubble and coral at the base of reef slopes.

region: Western Pacific — southern Japan & Taiwan to the Great Barrier Reef & New Caledonia
description: Deep electric blue with a bright yellow band along the back from the snout to the yellow tail. A deeper-water species of outer reef slopes, so it is less often collected than its shallow relatives.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Fiji
description: White with three bold black bars — through the eye, behind the head and across the rear body. It lives over rubble and sand on reef slopes, sheltering in small holes.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Andaman Sea to northern Sumatra
description: Brilliant blue with yellow on the rear of the belly, the anal fin and the lower part of the tail; also called the Andaman damsel. Small groups live over reef slopes and it is one of the gentler Pomacentrus.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Andaman Sea to the Line & Tuamotu Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Brilliant neon blue with yellow on the belly, anal fin and tail; common on rubble slopes, where loose groups feed on plankton just above the bottom.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Christmas Island & Indonesia to the Solomon Islands
description: Electric blue with a broad golden-yellow belly that continues onto the anal and tail fins; very like the neon damsel but with more yellow. Common around coral heads in lagoons.

region: Western Indian Ocean — East Africa & Madagascar to the Maldives & Chagos
description: The Indian Ocean counterpart of the neon damsel: sky-blue with a yellow belly and tail. Groups hover over rubble and coral and dive into crevices when threatened.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Iridescent greenish-blue with fine darker vertical lines and a small black spot on the upper gill cover. Groups live around isolated coral heads on sandy lagoon floors.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Entirely lemon-yellow, sometimes with faint bluish lines on the face; it lives among branching corals in lagoons and on reef slopes.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Red Sea & East Africa to Madagascar & Mauritius
description: Bright sulphur-yellow with a conspicuous black spot at the base of the pectoral fin; common in the Red Sea around coral heads in lagoons and on reef flats.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Vanuatu, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: Pale yellow, often with a lavender tinge, and fine blue lines on the face; juveniles have a blue-ringed black eyespot on the soft dorsal fin. Lives in lagoons near isolated coral heads on sand.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Fiji & Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Dark charcoal-grey speckled with blue on the head and front, with a pale tail and a blue-ringed black eyespot on the soft dorsal fin. Inhabits shallow reef flats and is fiercely territorial.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Purple-blue on the head and back grading to yellow-orange below and behind, with electric-blue lines and spots on the face and a blue-ringed black eyespot on the soft dorsal fin. Usually solitary on clear outer reef slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Line & Marquesas Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: White with three bold black bars and black pelvic fins. Groups live in a single branching coral head and dive into it at the first sign of danger; like other humbugs it becomes very aggressive with age.

region: Western Pacific — Sumatra to Vanuatu, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: Like the humbug damselfish but with a fourth black band across the tail fin. Groups live in a single branching coral head and dive into it at the first sign of danger; like other humbugs it becomes very aggressive with age.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Line & Pitcairn Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Velvet black with a white spot on each upper flank and one on the forehead; the spots fade and the body greys as it grows. Juveniles often shelter in anemones alongside clownfish.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Cocos-Keeling Islands to Samoa, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Pale bluish-grey with dark-edged scales forming a fine net, a dark bar behind the head and a black-edged dorsal fin. Groups hover above branching corals and retreat into them when threatened.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea & Java
description: Pale grey-brown with a dark band behind the head, fine blue speckling on the face and a whitish tail. Groups shelter in branching corals, the Indian Ocean counterpart of the reticulated damsel.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Oman
description: Pale grey with blue-speckled cheeks, a dark-margined dorsal fin and black pelvic fins. Colonies live among the branches of Stylophora and Acropora corals.

region: Central Pacific — Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: Hawaii's domino damsel: grey to black with a large white blotch on each upper flank, bigger than that of the three-spot domino. Adults gather above the reef to feed on plankton.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia, the Philippines, Palau & Papua New Guinea
description: Juveniles are velvet black with electric-blue lines and a yellow bar behind the head; adults lose most of the blue and become dark brown. Lives on sheltered coastal reefs and grows aggressive with age.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Vanuatu, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia
description: Juveniles are pale with a yellow back and electric-blue-edged pelvic and anal fins (the "bowtie damsel"); adults turn uniformly black. Unusually for a damsel, adults feed largely on soft corals.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Andaman Sea to Vanuatu, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Juveniles are bright yellow with two black stripes; adults become olive-brown with a yellow rear and tail and a black mark at the pectoral fin base. Common on coastal and lagoon reefs.

region: Atlantic Ocean — tropical western Atlantic incl. the Caribbean & Gulf of Mexico, and the eastern Atlantic
description: Silvery-white with five black bars and a yellow wash over the back; bold groups patrol Caribbean reefs and harbours. Nesting males turn dark bluish while guarding patches of purple eggs on rock.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Line Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: The Indo-Pacific twin of the Atlantic sergeant major: pale with five black bars and a yellow upper back. It forms large, bold aggregations around reefs and jetties.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Tuamotus, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Silvery-white with five narrow black bars and a black stripe along each lobe of the forked tail, like open scissors. Large groups feed on plankton above reef edges.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda & Florida to Brazil, incl. the Gulf of Mexico & Caribbean
description: Juveniles are electric blue above and yellow below with a black eyespot on the dorsal fin; adults fade to dusky brown with a yellowish tail. A farming damsel that fiercely guards its patch of algae.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Dark brown to black on the front half and white behind, often with a yellow patch on the lower flank. Males defend nest sites on the reef and court passing females with looping dips and "signal jumps".

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Juveniles are bright yellow with black spots on the dorsal fin, tail base and pectoral base; adults turn dusky grey-brown. It farms algae lawns inside staghorn and boulder corals and attacks intruders many times its size.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas to Brazil
description: Blue on the back and head grading to yellow on the belly, with a black spot on the dorsal fin and another on top of the tail base; colours darken with age. Common in shallow rocky and reef habitats.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida & the Bahamas through the Gulf of Mexico & Caribbean
description: Juveniles are deep blue covered in brilliant blue spots ("jewelfish"); adults are dark brown with a bright yellow tail. It farms algae and grazes fire coral polyps on shallow reef crests.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Christmas Island to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Bright golden-yellow with tall, pointed dorsal and anal fins and a few blue lines on the face. It lives on steep outer reef slopes and lays its eggs on gorgonians and whip corals.

region: Western Pacific — Malaysia & Indonesia to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Pale greenish-white with broad, faint olive-green bars and yellowish fins. Groups live around branching staghorn corals in lagoons and on sheltered reefs.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia
description: Silvery greenish-grey with a yellow belly and pelvic fins, and dark margins on the tail lobes. Small groups feed on plankton near branching corals on clear reef slopes.

region: Eastern Pacific — Monterey Bay, California to Baja California, Mexico
description: California's state marine fish: adults are solid brilliant orange, juveniles red-orange with iridescent blue spots. Males cultivate a nest of red algae on rock and defend it vigorously.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Papua New Guinea, north to Japan; introduced in the Gulf of Mexico
description: Slender dark grey-brown with a black spot on the gill cover and yellowish-white tips to the rear fins and tail lobes. Large groups feed on plankton above coastal reefs; it has spread into the Gulf of Mexico as an invasive species.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Tonga, north to Taiwan, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Bluish-grey with a bright yellow tail and rear body and a small black spot on the gill cover. Groups hover above coral to feed on plankton and are mild for damsels.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Marshall & Society Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Dark olive-brown sprinkled with bright blue spots, with a paler yellowish tail. A strongly territorial algae farmer of shallow reef flats and slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Line & Tuamotu Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Shimmering pale blue-green; large aggregations hover above branching Acropora and vanish into it when threatened. Males prepare a nest in sand or rubble where several females lay their eggs.

region: Indo-Pacific — Seychelles & Maldives to the Line Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: Almost identical to the blue-green chromis but with a black spot at the base (axil) of the pectoral fin; the two often school together over the same coral heads.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Brilliant blue with black margins on the dorsal fin and tail lobes; loose schools feed on plankton high above Caribbean reefs. Recently moved to the genus Azurina by some authors.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Pitcairn Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: One of the smallest chromis, olive-yellow with rows of electric-blue spots running along the scale rows. Large groups hover close to the reef in surge-swept shallows.

region: Western & South Pacific — Coral Sea & New Caledonia to the Tuamotus
description: Front half dark grey-brown and rear half, including the tail, white, divided sharply at mid-body. Small groups hover above outer reef slopes.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: A small, pale tan-yellow chromis with a single black bar across the rear of the body and a white tail. Groups stay close to coral heads on lagoon and outer reefs.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & Pacific — Christmas Island to the Line & Tuamotu Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands
description: Dark brown to black with a sharply contrasting white tail base and tail fin, plus a black spot at the pectoral base. Common on clear outer reef slopes.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Red Sea & East Africa to the Maldives
description: Chocolate-brown over the front half and white behind, as if dipped in chocolate. Groups hover a short way above branching corals.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Juveniles are electric blue and adults a deep blue-violet; a Caribbean chromis of deeper reef slopes and ledges, often hovering near overhangs.

region: Eastern Pacific — Monterey Bay, California to central Baja California
description: A large, dark blue-grey chromis with black spots on the rear body and fins, abundant in Californian kelp forests where schools feed on plankton by day and shelter in crevices at night. Recently moved to the genus Azurina by some authors.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Fiji, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Huge shoals of orange females hover over reef edges, each harem guarded by a larger magenta male with a long third dorsal spine and a red spot on the pectoral fin. All start life as females; when a male is lost, the dominant female changes sex.

region: Central & western Pacific — Palau and the Marshall, Gilbert & Line Islands
description: Females are lavender-pink below with a bright yellow back and tail; males develop a deeper magenta body and a broad orange-yellow back. It feeds in loose groups above lagoon pinnacles and outer reefs, and is one of the hardier anthias in aquaria.

region: Indo-Pacific — Christmas Island to the Line Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Males are orange-gold with a brilliant red dorsal fin and a lavender stripe from the snout to the pectoral fin, which they flash in rapid display dives; females are plain peach-orange. Forms large aggregations above shallow reef crests.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Solomon Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Both sexes are deep purple: females have a yellow stripe along the back and yellow-edged tail lobes, while males have a fleshy, protruding upper lip. Originally described in the genus Mirolabrichthys ("marvellous-lipped fish").

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: Males are pinkish-magenta with a large, squarish purple-violet patch on the flank; females are orange-yellow with a lavender stripe along the side. Lives on steep outer reef walls, usually below 15 m.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa & the Maldives to the Andaman Sea & Christmas Island
description: Lavender-purple with a bright yellow back from the head to the deeply forked yellow tail; the sexes look alike. Large aggregations feed on plankton along reef drop-offs.

region: Indo-Pacific — Mauritius & the Maldives to the Hawaiian & Line Islands
description: Upper half orange-yellow and lower half pink-lavender in both sexes; males grow elongated second and third dorsal spines with yellow tips. Found on outer reef slopes from about 5 to 70 m.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Maldives to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: A deep-bodied anthias with a short, crescent-shaped tail that lives in sheltered lagoons and on inshore reefs; males are pink-red with a red spot on the dorsal fin. Considered one of the hardier anthias.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Maldives & Sri Lanka to the Andaman Sea
description: Males are fiery red-orange with a deep red dorsal fin; females are orange-yellow. An Indian Ocean anthias of outer reef slopes, usually found below 20 m.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Palau & the Marshall Islands
description: A small anthias of outer reef walls, usually below about 20 m; both sexes are pink with a yellow back, males showing more orange on the dorsal fin and long tail filaments.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Christmas Island & Indonesia to Fiji, north to Palau
description: Pink-lavender with a yellow back and red-tipped tail lobes. It lives on steep outer walls, often below 15 m, and is among the less quarrelsome anthias.

region: Western & central Pacific — Indonesia to French Polynesia, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Rich purple-violet overall; males develop a magenta-red dorsal fin and longer tail lobes. Large schools hover off steep outer reef walls.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Tuamotus, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Pink with a row of short red bars across the upper rear body — hence the trade name "tiger queen" — and red-edged tail lobes. Lives on outer reef walls, usually below 20 m, often near caves.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Vanuatu, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Males are yellowish-green with a red stripe from the eye to the pectoral fin and red-edged, trailing tail lobes; females are olive-yellow. Prefers shallow, current-swept reef tops.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Samoa, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Males are pink-red with a broad crimson bar on the mid-flank and red-tipped tail lobes; females are pinkish-orange with yellow on the back. Lives over rubble on reef slopes and in channels.

region: Pacific — Hawaii, Johnston Atoll & the islands of Polynesia
description: A deep-water anthias, usually found below about 30 m, with very long pelvic fins; males are pink-magenta with yellow on the back and dorsal fin. It needs cooler water and subdued light to thrive in aquaria.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Fiji, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Orange-yellow with a bold red stripe along the side from the eye to the tail; males have a red patch on the dorsal fin. A cave-loving anthias of deeper reefs, shyer than most.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Fiji & Tonga, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: Deep-bodied and pink-orange, each scale edged in yellow, with a yellow stripe from the eye; it hides under overhangs and in caves on steep walls rather than schooling in open water. The genus name reflects its mix of anthias and hawkfish features.

region: Western Indian Ocean — East Africa & Madagascar to the Maldives & Chagos
description: Also called the threadfin goldie: orange-gold with a lavender band below the eye; males develop a long filament on the dorsal fin and long trailing tail lobes. Vast shoals hover above reefs in the western Indian Ocean.

region: Eastern Atlantic & Mediterranean — Portugal to Angola, incl. the Mediterranean, Madeira & the Canaries
description: A deep-red Mediterranean anthias with yellow stripes on the head and very long pelvic fins; it lives in caves and under overhangs from about 15 m to well below 100 m. A favourite in European public aquaria.

region: Western Atlantic — the Bahamas & the Caribbean, from Belize to the Lesser Antilles
description: Deep purple with a black cap running from the snout over the top of the head into the front of the dorsal fin. A deeper-water relative of the royal gramma, usually found below 30 m in crevices and under ledges on reef walls.

region: Southwestern Atlantic — coast of Brazil
description: Brazil's counterpart of the royal gramma, separated from it by the outflow of the Amazon; it is likewise purple in front and yellow behind and shelters under ledges and in crevices.

region: Red Sea
description: Vivid orchid-purple with a thin dark line from the snout through the eye; it lives on vertical walls and under overhangs in the Red Sea. One of the least aggressive dottybacks, and widely captive-bred.

region: Northwestern Indian Ocean — Persian Gulf & Gulf of Oman to Pakistan & Sri Lanka; Aldabra
description: Bright orange with electric-blue lines through the eye and along the bases of the dorsal and anal fins. One of the most aggressive dottybacks, defending its cave against much larger fish; widely captive-bred.

region: Red Sea
description: Small and velvet black with electric-blue lines around the head and on the margins of the dorsal and anal fins. It shelters among branching corals and is widely captive-bred.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Brilliant blue with a bright yellow back running from the snout to the yellow tail. It lives around sandy patches and the bases of reefs and is widely captive-bred.

region: Southern Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Black with two bold white stripes along the body. Unusually for a dottyback it lives in small groups among corals, and captive-bred fish can often be kept together.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia (Bali, Lombok, Flores & Komodo)
description: Males are dark grey with an orange-yellow head and a red-orange tail, earning the "firetail" name; females are plain grey-brown. One of the larger Pseudochromis and quite aggressive.

region: Indo-West Pacific — India & Sri Lanka to Vanuatu, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia
description: Strikingly variable, from dusky brown to bright yellow (sold as the golden dottyback). On the reef it can shift colour to match nearby damselfishes, a mimicry that helps it ambush juvenile fish.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden to the Persian Gulf
description: Olive-brown with a small blue spot on each scale and a blue-ringed dark spot on the gill cover. A hardy dottyback of shallow reef crevices.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Vanuatu & New Caledonia
description: Magenta-purple in front and yellow behind, often with a thin white line where the colours meet; easily mistaken for the royal gramma but without its black dorsal spot. Formerly placed in Pseudochromis.

region: Western Pacific — the Philippines & Indonesia to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands
description: Solid magenta-purple, sold as the strawberry dottyback; small but pugnacious towards fish of similar shape. Formerly Pseudochromis porphyreus.

region: Western Pacific — Malaysia & the Philippines
description: Bright yellow with a magenta-purple band running from the snout along the back into the dorsal fin. It lives among coral rubble and branching corals on sheltered reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Ryukyu Islands and northern Australia
description: A large, heavy-bodied dottyback, also called the fire-tail devil: males are deep red with dark lines along the scale rows and blue-edged fins, females duller orange-brown. An aggressive predator of small fishes and crustaceans on shallow rocky reefs.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Western Australia
description: Endemic to Western Australia: orange-red to yellow with many fine dark blue lines along the body and blue-edged fins. A large, aggressive predator best kept with robust tankmates.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Males are orange-red with oblique purple lines along the scale rows and purplish fins; females are mostly purple-red. A shy species that seldom leaves its crevices on outer reef slopes.

region: Western Pacific — Great Barrier Reef & Coral Sea to New Caledonia
description: Deep blue with a forked tail; small groups hover upside down beneath ledges and in caves, oriented to the rock overhead. The male broods the eggs in his mouth.

region: Western Pacific — northern Great Barrier Reef & Coral Sea
description: The bright yellow relative of the blue assessor; it likewise hangs upside down in caves and under ledges, and the male mouthbroods the eggs.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Line Islands & Tonga, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Dark brown covered in small white-blue spots, with huge rounded fins and an eyespot at the rear of the dorsal fin; when threatened it pokes its head into a crevice so its tail end mimics the head of a white-mouth moray. Males guard the egg clusters.

region: Indonesia — Banggai Islands, central Sulawesi
description: Silver with three black bars, white-spotted black fins and tall, flag-like dorsal fins; groups hover among long-spined sea urchins and anemones in shallow bays. The male broods the eggs in his mouth for about a month and releases fully formed juveniles; endangered in the wild, it is now widely captive-bred.

region: Western Pacific — Java & the Philippines to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Yellow-tan head with bright red eyes, a broad dark brown band across the middle and a pale rear body peppered with orange-red spots. Groups hover among branching corals by day and hunt small crustaceans at night.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Kiribati, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: Silvery-grey with a thin dark bar below the first dorsal fin and scattered small dark spots on the rear body. It lives among mangrove roots and in sheltered harbours and tolerates brackish water.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: A small, translucent cardinalfish with iridescent blue streaks on the head, an orange line through the eye and a long, thread-like first dorsal spine. Schools hover among branching corals in sheltered lagoons.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Marshall Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Silvery-blue with six bright orange-yellow stripes along the body. By day groups shelter in crevices, among coral branches or between sea-urchin spines, emerging at dusk to feed.

region: Western Pacific — Malaysia & Indonesia to the Solomon Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Pale silvery body with ochre-brown stripes and large blue-tinged eyes; juveniles carry a black spot at the tail base. Small groups hover among branching corals by day.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Tonga, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Golden-copper with two blue lines on the face and a broad black ring around the tail base. Groups shelter in caves and under ledges by day.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Tuamotus, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Pale yellowish-white with five broad black stripes running from the snout to the tail. Shy and nocturnal, it shelters in crevices on reef slopes by day.

region: Western Atlantic — New England & Bermuda to Brazil, incl. the Gulf of Mexico & Caribbean
description: Bright red with a black spot below the second dorsal fin, a dark saddle on the tail base and two white lines through the eye. It hides in crevices by day and hunts small crustaceans at night.

region: Eastern Atlantic & Mediterranean — Portugal to the Gulf of Guinea, incl. Madeira, the Canaries & Cape Verde
description: The Mediterranean's native cardinalfish: orange-red with very large eyes, it hides in caves and crevices by day and hunts at night. As in its relatives, the male carries the egg mass in his mouth.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Pitcairn Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia
description: Pale with five thin black stripes and a yellow patch with a black spot on the tail base. Armed with long canine teeth, it hunts small fishes and crustaceans at night.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
description: Translucent pinkish with a broad black girdle around the rear body below the second dorsal fin. Schools hover close to branching corals in sheltered lagoons; formerly placed in the genus Archamia.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — Red Sea to Hawaii, and the Gulf of California to Colombia
description: White with a crimson checkerboard grid and a very long snout used to pluck tiny crustaceans from the gorgonians and black corals on which it perches, usually below 10 m. A notorious jumper.

region: Pacific — Ryukyu Islands to the Great Barrier Reef, east to the Line, Mangareva & Austral Islands
description: Brilliant scarlet with a black band along the base of the dorsal fin and a dark ring around the eye. It lives deep among the branches of Pocillopora and Stylophora corals.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Recognised by a U-shaped band of orange, red and blue curving behind the eye; body colour varies from pinkish-brown to olive, often with a white stripe on the rear flank. Perches on branching corals.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to the Line & Ducie Islands, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Head and front body densely freckled with small dark spots, with a broad dark band along the upper rear flank and a pale belly. It ambushes small fishes and shrimps from coral heads and is larger and bolder than most hawkfishes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Maldives to Samoa, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
description: A small white hawkfish with red-brown saddle bars that break into spots below, and tufts of cirri on the tips of its dorsal spines. It perches on coral heads and darts out at passing crustaceans.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — Red Sea to the Marquesas, and the Gulf of California to Colombia
description: Pale with large clustered blotches of red, brown or olive that vary with habitat (also sold as the pixy hawkfish). It perches on corals and rocks and darts out at small crustaceans.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Indonesia to Fiji, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: White to pink with large reddish-brown blotches in rough rows, a dark spot on the gill cover and fringed dorsal spines. Usually perches on sponges and soft corals.

region: Western Pacific & Indian Ocean — southern Japan & China to Indonesia; India
description: Golden-yellow to orange with faint darker blotches; a rarely exported hawkfish of rocky reefs, mostly collected in southern Japan.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Tonga, north to Japan, south to New Caledonia
description: The only hawkfish that habitually swims in open water: it hovers in currents to snatch plankton, resting on rocks or sponges between feeds. Orange-tan with a lyre-shaped tail.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas through the Caribbean to Brazil
description: White with five dark brown bars, tiny red spots over the head and back, and a black spot on the soft dorsal fin and tail base. A small Caribbean hawkfish that perches among rocks and corals.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas through the Caribbean to Venezuela
description: Also called the peppermint bass: red-orange with dark red-brown stripes alternating with yellow, and black blotches on the second dorsal, anal and tail fins. A secretive cave-dweller that seldom leaves deep reef crevices.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida Keys, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Alternating orange and lavender stripes with blue-ringed black spots on the second dorsal fin and tail lobes. It lives deep in crevices on reef walls, usually below 15 m, and is one of the most expensive Caribbean aquarium fishes.

region: Western Atlantic — North Carolina to Florida & the Gulf of Mexico
description: Salmon-pink with a broad dark brown stripe from the snout to the tail, bordered above and below by yellow lines. It lives in crevices on deep ledges and hard-bottom reefs off the south-eastern United States.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida & the Bahamas through the Caribbean
description: White with bold black bars and blotches forming a tiger pattern, a pointed snout and yellow-tinged fins. A simultaneous hermaphrodite — each fish is both male and female — that hunts small fishes and shrimps near the bottom.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas through the Caribbean
description: Orange-tan with pale blue to lavender bars along the side; small aggregations hover a short way above rubble to feed on zooplankton. Like other Serranus it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite.

region: Eastern Atlantic & Mediterranean — Bay of Biscay to Senegal, incl. the Mediterranean & Black Sea
description: Reddish-brown with dark bars, a blue patch on the belly and squiggly blue "writing" on the head, which gives it its name (scriba = scribe). A bold ambush predator of Mediterranean rocky reefs and seagrass meadows.

region: Western Atlantic — North Carolina to Florida & the Gulf of Mexico
description: Brown with darker bars, a white belt across the belly and a black blotch on the dorsal fin. A small, bold simultaneous hermaphrodite of jetties, rocky bottoms and reefs.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Pale yellowish-white with a black saddle on the tail base and blue and black markings on the snout. Like all hamlets it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite: paired fish take turns releasing eggs and sperm at dusk.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida, the Bahamas & the western Caribbean
description: White with five broad indigo-blue bars and blue pelvic fins. Like all hamlets it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite: paired fish take turns releasing eggs and sperm at dusk.

region: Western Atlantic — southern Florida & the Florida Keys
description: Brilliant blue all over, with black margins along the upper and lower tail lobes; found almost only in southern Florida. Like all hamlets it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite: paired fish take turns releasing eggs and sperm at dusk.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Pale yellowish-tan with dark brown bars, the central one widest, and blue lines on the head; the most common hamlet on many Caribbean reefs. Like all hamlets it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite: paired fish take turns releasing eggs and sperm at dusk.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Dark blue-black to brownish-black all over; it hunts small fishes and shrimps close to coral cover. Like all hamlets it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite: paired fish take turns releasing eggs and sperm at dusk.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida, the Bahamas & the Caribbean
description: Bright yellow on the head, belly and fins with a dark blue-black patch over the upper body; it stays close to cover, hence its name. Like all hamlets it is a simultaneous hermaphrodite: paired fish take turns releasing eggs and sperm at dusk.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Palau, Papua New Guinea & the Solomon Islands
description: A tiny, hawkfish-like perchlet that sits propped on its fins on rock, white with a geometric pattern of red-orange to brown blocks along its side. It lives in reef crevices at roughly 10–65 m.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas to Barbados & Venezuela
description: Pale blue-white with a yellow head; it hovers vertically above a stone-lined burrow it builds itself, picking plankton, and drops back into the hole tail-first. Males incubate the eggs in their mouths.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California, Mexico
description: Golden-yellow to tan covered in electric-blue spots; courting males rise from their burrows with fins spread, turning dark with brilliant blue spots. Lives in colonies on sand slopes in the Sea of Cortez.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas through the Caribbean
description: Mottled tan and brown with darker bands and an enormous mouth whose jaws extend well behind the eye. It ambushes small fishes and crustaceans from its burrow, and males mouthbrood large egg masses.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas through the Caribbean to Brazil
description: A small, mottled brown jawfish with paler blotches; it lives in burrows in sand and rubble near reefs, and males brood the eggs in their mouths.

region: Western Pacific — the Philippines & Indonesia
description: Tan with fine dark mottling, a black spot on the spiny dorsal fin and golden markings around the eyes like spectacles. It digs burrows in sand and rubble, and the male mouthbroods the eggs.

region: Western Pacific — the Philippines & Indonesia to Papua New Guinea & northern Australia
description: Grey-green covered with large black eyespots ringed in orange and green, set in a fine tracery of blue and orange lines. Like the mandarin it feeds almost entirely on tiny copepods picked from rock, so it needs a mature tank.

region: Western Pacific — Japan to Australia, east to the Marquesas & Pitcairn Islands
description: Mottled red-brown and white; males raise a tall, flag-like first dorsal fin marked with dark eyespots. Often sold as the scooter dragonet, it hops across sand and rubble picking up copepods and amphipods.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Tonga, north to Japan, south to Australia
description: Pale with bright red-brown mottling and fine white flecks; males have a tall first dorsal fin with black blotches. A hardy hunter of copepods and amphipods, often sold as the red scooter dragonet.

region: Western Pacific — southern Japan to the Philippines & Indonesia
description: Red-orange mottled with white; males sport an extremely tall, sail-like first dorsal fin that they raise in display to rivals and females. It lives on rubble and sand of coastal reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Palau, Papua New Guinea & northern Australia
description: A large sand-dwelling dragonet that "walks" on finger-like free pelvic rays; males raise an enormous, colourful first dorsal fin in display. It buries in sand and feeds on small invertebrates.
